why: Near-identical violins; A's median labels (with units) sit above the strip points while B's '3,700' labels sit on top of the dots.
Near-identical panels; B uses clean integer day ticks (0,5,...,20) instead of A's fussy 2.5-step ticks, and shows x ticks on every panel.
B colours Europe and Africa in the same red (and Americas in a near-red salmon), so continents are hard to tell apart, while A's six hues are distinct.
B's subtitle is visibly broken by a mathtext bug ('6to230' in italics) and makes a dubious claim, whereas A is clean apart from a pale-yellow AMZN line.
Near-identical; B's median labels have a halo and read cleanly over the points, while A's '5,000 g' and '3,700 g' are partly obscured by darker dots (A's subtitle is marginally more accurate).
Essentially identical; A starts the shared y-axis at 0, giving an honest growth baseline.
Essentially identical; A labels the no-skill baseline value (0.68) and states the average AUC in the footer.
A colours Europe and Africa in the same red and Asia in a near-red orange, while B gives every continent a distinct hue, making the colour encoding readable.
B's log scale untangles the four low-priced stocks that A crushes into an unreadable band near zero, though B has sparse $10/$100 ticks and a peak label crowding the subtitle.
